Part 3
Questions 19 to 26
You are going to read an extract from a narrative recount. For questions 19 - 26, choose the
correct answer (A, B, C or D) and mark the correct letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet.
The wind carried a sharp, salty scent as Maya zipped up her jacket and stepped onto
the beach, the cold biting through the fabric as clouds gathered overhead. Although her
mother had asked her to stay home and help clean, Maya had stormed out after an argument,
needing air and needing space. The beach was usually her escape. But this morning,
something felt different – tense, unsettled, as if the sea were holding its breath. Then she saw
it.
At first, it looked like driftwood. But as she got closer, her heart lurched. Lying
motionless on the wet sand was a turtle – large, battered, and barely breathing. Its dull eyes
stared ahead, and one flipper twitched weakly. Kneeling beside it, Maya saw a long strip of
plastic dangling from its mouth, half-buried in the sand. Her throat tightened. She
remembered a documentary they had watched in class: turtles mistaking plastic for jellyfish,
dying slowly as it blocked their insides.
She reached into her pocket and grabbed her phone. No signal. Panic stirred. She
gently tugged the plastic. The turtle flinched and let out a low, pitiful sound. It was lodged
deep. Her mind raced. If she ran for help, it might be too late. If she stayed, she could not do
anything.
Then she remembered: an old lifeguard hut stood near the cove, about ten minutes
away. “I’ll be back,” she whispered, brushing sand off the shell. “Hold on.”
She ran. Sand flew beneath her shoes as the wind picked up and rain began to fall.
Her lungs burned, but she did not stop. The hut was locked, dark. Her heart sank, but then she
spotted a red emergency box on the wall. Inside, a two-way radio. She pressed the button, her
voice shaking.
“This is Maya. I’m at South Point Beach. A turtle is stranded with plastic in its mouth.
It’s alive but weak. Please, send help.”
Static. Then a voice crackled through: “Message received. Rescue team en route. Stay
with the animal.”
8 MODUL KECEMERLANGAN BAHASA INGGERIS SEKOLAH MENENGAH NEGERI JOHOR

She ran back, soaked and breathless. The turtle had not moved much. She knelt beside
it, shielding its head with her jacket, whispering softly, though she did not know if it
understood.
Minutes passed. Then, flashing lights appeared on the horizon, followed by the hum
of an engine. Two rescuers rushed toward her with gear and a stretcher.
“You did well,” one said, crouching beside her. “It still has a chance.” They worked
quickly, gently lifting the turtle and checking its breathing. Another rescuer nodded.
“Swallowed plastic. But we’ve seen worse. It’s going to the marine centre.” As the van
disappeared into the rain, Maya remained where she was, the waves crashing beside her.
Somewhere beyond the shore, more creatures like this one swam through polluted waters,
unseen.
That night, after a hot shower and dinner, she sat at her desk and began to type. Not
for school. Not for likes. Just a truth that pressed on her chest:
“We are part of nature, not separate from it. What we throw away doesn’t vanish; it
returns. Sometimes in the mouth of an innocent animal. If we stay silent, nothing changes.
But if we speak, maybe something will.”
She didn’t know if the turtle would live. But she had spoken, and maybe that was
where change began.

The Importance of Spending Money Wisely
Spending money is something we all do, whether it is for food, clothes or
entertainment. However, it is important to spend money wisely. This means thinking
carefully before buying something and making sure it is something you really need. When
you spend money in a smart way, you can save more and avoid stress later. Being wise with
your money can also help you feel more in control of your life.
One of the first steps to spending money wisely is knowing the difference between
needs and wants. Needs are things you must have, such as food, shelter and clothes. Wants
are things you would like to have but can live without, like a new branded phone or
expensive shoes. 27 This question can help you avoid wasting money on things you
do not need.
Another good habit is making a budget. A budget is a plan that shows how much
money you get and how much you can spend. When you make a budget, you can decide how
much to spend on different things, like school supplies, food and fun activities. 28 A
simple budget can help you stay organised and prevent you from running out of money too
soon.
It is a good idea to learn how to handle money from a young age. 29 For
example, giving children a small amount of pocket money can teach them how to manage
their spending. When young people learn how to save and spend wisely early in life, they are
more likely to become responsible adults.
Not spending money wisely can lead to many problems. 30 This can cause
stress and even debt. For instance, if someone always buys new clothes but forgets to pay for
school fees or food, they may end up in trouble. That is why it is important to think carefully
before spending.

There are many ways to become a smart shopper. One tip is to compare prices before
you buy something. 31 Another tip is to wait for sales or discounts. Buying during
sales can help you save a lot of money. Also, try to pay with cash instead of a credit card, so
you are more aware of how much you are spending.
Saving money is just as important as spending wisely. 32 You can save for
future needs like school trips, gifts or emergencies. Having some money saved gives you
peace of mind and more choices. You do not need to save a lot at once; even small amounts
add up over time.
In conclusion, spending money wisely is an important life skill. It helps you make
better choices, avoid financial problems and prepare for the future. Whether you are young or
old, it is never too late to start. With simple steps like budgeting, saving and shopping
carefully, you can take control of your money and use it in the best way possible.

Part 5
Questions 33 to 40
We interviewed six people about famous sports in Malaysia. Read the texts below and answer
the questions that follow.
FAMOUS SPORTS IN MALAYSIA
A – Football
Football is one of the most talked about sports in Malaysia. Teenagers like to play football
after school or during the weekend. They also watch football matches on TV or online.
Some support local teams, like JDT and Sri Pahang, while others cheer for big clubs like
Manchester United or Barcelona. They think football is exciting and fast, and it helps them
stay active. Some say playing football teaches cooperation among teammates and
discipline.
B – Badminton
Badminton is another local favourite among many teens in Malaysia. This is because our
country has famous players like Pearly Tan and Aaron Chia who have won medals in
international competitions. Malaysia is recognised as one of the top countries in this sport,
standing alongside China and Japan. Some students take badminton seriously and join
training classes. Others play just for fun with friends.
C – Basketball
Basketball is becoming more popular among Malaysian teenagers, especially in urban
areas. They like the fast pace and high energy of the game. Many schools have basketball
teams, and students take part in competitions. Teenagers think basketball helps them make
friends and build confidence. A few teenagers follow the NBA and admire famous players
like LeBron James or Stephen Curry.
D – Swimming
Some Malaysian teenagers enjoy swimming, especially those living near the coast or with
access to pools. Swimming is a form of relaxation and fun. It is also a good way to stay fit
without getting too hot. Swimming is popular in school sports programmes, and some
teenagers join swimming clubs. They believe it improves breathing, strength, and body
control. A few students aspire to become professional swimmers one day.
13 MODUL KECEMERLANGAN BAHASA INGGERIS SEKOLAH MENENGAH NEGERI JOHOR

E – E-sports (Electronic Sports)
E-sports have become a major industry, and are a crowd favourite among teenagers. It has
slowly grown from local events to a worldwide phenomenon, mainly thanks to the internet.
Malaysian teenagers play video games like Mobile Legends or Valorant. Teenagers enjoy
joining online tournaments and watching streamers or top players. However, some parents
worry that playing too much might affect schoolwork and health.
F – Martial Arts
Silat, taekwondo, and karate are examples of martial arts that are also liked by teenagers in
Malaysia. They say these sports help them feel strong and focused. Many schools offer
martial arts classes or clubs to encourage students to take part in competitions and win
medals in the future. Teenagers learn not just how to defend themselves, but also how to
respect others. They enjoy the commitment and training routines.
